title: The Tidekeepers at Dusk
summary: On an island where the tide returns lost memories, a young keeper must decide which histories deserve to stay buried.
review: Solenne gives this quiet, salt-bright fantasy a remarkable sense of place. Its magic is never more moving than when it asks what a community owes its past.

title: A Map of Small Rooms
summary: Three siblings return to their childhood apartment to decide what to keep, and discover how differently they remember it.
review: North's precise, generous prose makes domestic details feel quietly monumental. A thoughtful novel about inheritance that avoids easy answers.

title: The Last Light in Merrow
summary: A lighthouse ledger turns up after a storm, linking a present-day disappearance to a keeper who vanished decades earlier.
review: Wells makes a small harbor feel like a puzzle with weather. The reveals are earned, and the final pages land with real emotional weight.

title: Field Notes for a Changing Sky
summary: A naturalist travels through six threatened landscapes to learn what local caretakers notice first.
review: Arora pairs clear reporting with a deep respect for the people doing patient work. The book is candid about loss without surrendering its curiosity.

title: The Orbit Between Us
summary: Two engineers on a remote station inherit a failing habitat and one very complicated message from home.
review: Tanaka keeps the engineering details legible and the characters delightfully human. A warm, tense story about building trust under pressure.

title: Letters from Briar House
summary: A practical estate gardener and an impulsive letter writer clash over the future of a neglected country house.
review: Rowe brings wit and tenderness to a familiar setup, with two leads who grow in believable directions. The letters are a particular pleasure.

title: The Quiet Engine
summary: In a city powered by shared dreams, a technician begins to hear the same unknown voice each night.
review: An inventive premise with an understated, humane center. The world-building is strongest in the small rituals people invent to feel safe.

title: What the River Keeps
summary: A local reporter revisits a decades-old ferry accident when a name appears in the river's seasonal census.
review: A patient mystery with a keen ear for a town's competing versions of itself. The answer matters, but so does how the questions are asked.

title: An Inventory of Morning
summary: A baker begins recording the neighborhood sounds before dawn and finds an unexpected way back to her estranged brother.
review: North finds a lovely structure in repeated mornings and small acts of attention. A compact, affecting novel that trusts its readers.

title: The House of Second Weather
summary: A house changes its rooms with the seasons, sheltering travelers who each carry a promise they cannot keep.
review: A richly imagined ensemble story about hospitality and change. The episodic shape gives every guest room to surprise us.

title: A Practical History of Clouds
summary: An accessible tour of how communities have read, measured, and lived beneath the changing sky.
review: The best chapters connect scientific shifts to everyday decisions. Arora's enthusiasm is infectious, and the illustrations are described with care.

title: The Long Way to June
summary: Two rival train conductors share a route, a broken timetable, and an increasingly difficult reason to say goodbye.
review: A charming slow burn with a wonderfully specific setting. Rowe balances the travel mishaps with a sincere story about choosing a direction together.
